annotations.title: Hand the app to a client

description: For an app the person built for someone else (a client): the client claims it onto their own account, and from then on their plan pays for it and it is theirs. Deploy it signed in first (`login`), so it is on the person's own account; then call this. With `email`, the claim link is emailed to the client and only that address can claim it; without, give the returned `claim_url` to the person to send themselves (never open or claim it yourself). Until it is claimed it stays on the person's account and their plan pays; if nobody claims it within 7 days (`claim_by`) it is removed, so tell the person that date. Calling it again makes a new link (the old one stops) without moving the date. `keep: true` keeps it on the person's own account instead: no longer a client's, nothing removes it. After the claim the person can go on deploying it, changing settings and reading logs; removing it, inviting people and paid extras are then the client's. `category` files it in the person's own folder (made if new). Without this tool, `npx uarpie client jane@example.com --category "Acme Ltd"` does the same.

category.description: The person's own folder for it, for example the client's name. Made if it is new.

email.description: The client's email: the link is sent there, and only that address can claim it.

keep.description: true: keep it on the person's own account instead of handing it over.

project.description: Project id (prj_…) or the app's name (slug). Defaults to the project in deploy.json in the current directory.
